data.long_meaning: Derived from the Persian words ‘azar’ meaning gold and ‘aksh’ meaning eyes or hair, Azarakhsh is a name of royal and celestial origin. In the Islamic tradition, it is said that Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) praised this name and its bearer would be blessed with wisdom and a strong spiritual connection. The name Azarakhsh carries the meaning “Golden-haired, radiant” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Azarakhsh usually hope their child will grow to embody golden-haired, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Azarakhsh was the name of a powerful vizier (advisor) in the court of the Seljuq Sultan Sanjar (1087-1118 CE), known for his wisdom and bravery. He was a crucial figure during the Seljuq Empire's struggle against the Crusaders and other adversaries.

Azarakhsh is also mentioned in the Persian epic poem 'The Conference of the Birds' by Farid al-Din Attar (1145-1221 CE), where it refers to a spiritual guide or master. The poem is a mystical allegory describing a group of birds in search of their king, Simurgh.
